data.gender_notes: Hemangi is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Hemangi is derived from the Sanskrit word 'hemang', which means 'sun' and 'anga' meaning 'ray'. The name Hemangi symbolizes the sun's rays that light up the world. The name Hemangi carries the meaning “Sun Ray” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Hemangi usually hope their child will grow to embody sun ray and live with faith, good character and purpose.

Historically, the name has been popular in Indian communities and is associated with the elegant and rich culture of India. The name Hemangi conjures images of glowing skin, golden sunsets, and vibrant hues, making it a fitting name for a child born into a Hindu family.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, the sun represents the divine force of life and consciousness. The name Hemangi is considered auspicious as it is derived from the Sanskrit word 'hemang', which honors the symbolic power of the sun's rays. The name Hemangi invokes the idea of illuminating the world with one's presence, bringing light and positivity wherever one goes. data.spiritual_symbolism: Hemangi: Goddess of beauty and grace in Hindu mythology, symbolizing the radiant inner light of an individual. Her name signifies the adornment of the heart with love and compassion.

vedic_reference.note: The name Hemangi is not directly derived from any Vedic text or mythology. However, it is composed of two Sanskrit words: 'hem' meaning 'gem' and 'mangi' meaning 'beloved'. These words have been used in various Hindu texts and mythologies to describe various deities and concepts.

historical_references.reference: Hemangi was the name of a renowned poetess and a courtier in the court of king Bhoja of Dhar, in present-day Madhya Pradesh, India. She is believed to have flourished around the 11th century AD and is known for her beautiful Sanskrit verses, which were often on the theme of love and devotion to the god Krishna.
historical_references.context: Renowned poetess and courtier in the court of king Bhoja of Dhar, known for her beautiful Sanskrit verses on love and devotion to god Krishna.

historical_references.reference: Hemangi is also mentioned in the Indian epic Mahabharata as the name of the eldest wife of Bhishma Pitamaha. The context suggests that Hemangi was the first of the fifty-two wives of Bhishma, who was the grandsire of the Pandavas and the Kauravas.
